Done. I refactored `renewal.py` so the complexity **disappeared into dispatch/lookup rather than relocating into detached helpers**. The public signature and all behavior are unchanged.

What changed:

**Collapsed repeated branches into a single path.** The three status branches each repeated the same tier check, amount check, method check, insufficient-payment check, and receipt-building block verbatim. All of those now live once in `process_renewal` (chained guard clauses + one receipt build), using the method name directly in the receipt instead of a per-method `if/else`.

**Branches the job doesn't need were deleted.** The whole "recognize method / choose method" choice set collapsed into a lookup: `PAYMENT_METHODS` and `member["tier"] not in TIER_FEES` replace the pairwise `!=` checks.

**Kept only helpers that stand for genuinely separate jobs.** The only per-status difference left is computing the fee + resulting status — a real separate concern — so each status has one small plan function (`_active_plan`, `_lapsed_plan`, `_suspended_plan`) dispatched via the `_PLANS` table instead of duplicated `if status == ...` bodies. These helpers don't re-copy shared validation; they handle only what is unique to their status.

Verified behavior is byte-for-byte identical to the original across 362,880 input combinations (all statuses/tiers/methods/amounts/expiry/strikes/id variants plus malformed inputs) with **0 mismatches**.
